Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verses 1–2:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise (1). To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent (2).﴾

The meaning of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah﴾ is that every creature beneath Him glorifies Him, exalting Him, affirming His lordship, and submitting in obedience to Him, just as He, the Majestic in praise, said: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification.﴾

* *

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾

He says: But He, the Majestic, is the Almighty in His retribution against those who disobey Him, opposing His command from among His creatures in the heavens and the earth. ﴿The All-Wise﴾ in His management of their affairs and His disposal of them in whatever He wills and loves.

* *

And His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾

He, the Exalted in remembrance, says: To Him belongs the authority over the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and nothing in them is able to resist Him. His command is executed over all of them, and His judgment is carried out.

* *

And His saying: ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾

He says: He gives life to whatever He wills of creation, by bringing it into being as He wills, namely by bringing a living creature out of a dead drop of semen, by breathing the spirit into it after successive stages through which He transforms it, and similar things. And He causes to die whatever He wills of the living after life, when it reaches its appointed term, so He annihilates it. ﴿And He is over all things competent﴾: He, the Majestic in praise, says: He is possessed of power over every thing; nothing He wills is beyond His reach, whether giving life or causing death, honoring or humbling, or other matters.

The commentary on the Qur'an by al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verses 3–4:

The exegesis (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward, and He is Knowing of all things (3). He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do (4).﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿He is the First﴾ before everything, without any limit; ﴿and the Last﴾, meaning: the Last after everything, without any end. This was said in this way because He existed when nothing else existed besides Him, and He will exist after all things perish, as He, may His majesty be exalted, said: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and the Outward﴾

meaning: He is the Outward over everything other than Him, and He is the High above everything, so nothing is higher than Him. ﴿And the Inward﴾ meaning: He is the Inward of all things, so nothing is nearer to a thing than He is, as He said: ﴿And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein﴾.

What we have said about this has been reported in a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) held this view.

Mention of those who said this, and the report that was narrated concerning it:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Outward and the Inward﴾: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his companions when a cloud gathered over them, and he said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the ar-Raqi' (the canopy), a moving wave that is held back, and a protected ceiling." He said: "Do you know how far it is between you and it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is five hundred years' journey." He said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said the same. He said: "Above it is another sky, and between them is a five hundred years' journey." He said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said the same as their first answer. He said: "Above that is the Throne, and between it and the seventh sky is like the distance between the two skies." He said: "Do you know what is beneath you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the earth." He said: "Do you know what is beneath it?" They gave him the same answer as their first. He said: "Beneath it is another earth, and between them is a five hundred years' journey," until he counted seven earths, between each two earths a five hundred years' journey. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if one of you were lowered by a rope to the lower earth, he would descend upon Allah." Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Outward and the Inward, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and He is Knowing of all things﴾

meaning, may His remembrance be exalted: He is possessed of knowledge of everything; nothing is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heavens is absent from Him, nor anything smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a Clear Record.

* *

And His saying: ﴿He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾

meaning, may His remembrance be exalted: He is the One who brought into being the seven heavens and the earths, and arranged them and what is in them, then established Himself upon His Throne, rising above it and exalting Himself over it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it﴾

meaning, may His remembrance be exalted, informing about His attribute, and that nothing hidden among His creatures is concealed from Him: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾ of His creatures. By His saying ﴿yalij﴾ he means: enters. ﴿And what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky﴾ to the earth of anything at all. ﴿And what ascends into it﴾, so that it rises up into it from the earth. ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾, meaning: He is a witness over you, O people, wherever you are, knowing you, and knowing your deeds, your movements and your dwelling places, while He is upon His Throne above His seven heavens. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, meaning: Allah, with respect to your deeds that you perform, whether good or evil, obedience or disobedience, is possessed of sight, and He takes account of them, so that He may recompense the good-doer among you for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil, ﴿that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 8:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are [truly] believers?﴾ (57:8)

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not believe in Allah﴾, meaning: What is your situation, O people, that you do not affirm the oneness of Allah, while His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) invites you to acknowledge His oneness, and proofs have already come to you confirming the truth of that, proofs which have cut off your excuse and removed doubt from your hearts? ﴿And He has already taken your covenant﴾. It has been said: this refers to the following: your Lord has already taken your covenant from you in the loins of Adam, that Allah is your Lord and that there is no god for you besides Him.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And He has already taken your covenant﴾, he said: "In the back of Adam."

The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, except Abu Amr, recited ﴿وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثَاقَكُمْ﴾ with a fatha on the alif of akhadha and the mithaq in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: "And your Lord has already taken your covenant." Abu Amr recited it ﴿وَقَدْ أُخِذَ مِيثَاقُكُمْ﴾ with a damma on the alif and the mithaq in the nominative (raf'), in the passive form (ʿalā wajh mā lam yusamma fāʿiluh), where the agent is not named.

The correct view on this is that they are two readings close in meaning; whichever one the reciter reads is correct. However, the reading with a fatha on the alif of akhadha and the mithaq in the accusative is more pleasing to me among the two readings, because of its wide recitation and the rarity of recitation with the other.

* *

And His words: ﴿if you are [truly] believers﴾

He says: If you intend to believe in Allah at any time, then now is the most fitting time, so that the proofs may follow one another upon you through the Messenger, his informing you, his calling you to what you have already been certain of through the information, the evidence, and the covenant taken from you.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And indeed Allah, by His sending down to His servant what He sent down to him of clear signs for your guidance and for making you see the right path, is truly full of kindness (ra'fah) and mercy toward you. From His kindness and mercy toward you, He did that.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah, and to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to each Allah has promised the best. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (10)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And what is wrong with you, O people, that you do not spend from what Allah has provided you in the way of Allah? Your wealth will return to Allah if you do not spend it in your lifetime in the way of Allah, for to Him belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. He, may His majesty be exalted, urged them to their own benefit by saying to them: Spend your wealth in the way of Allah, so that this may be a store for you with Allah before you die, and you will not be able to do so, and the wealth will become an inheritance for the one to whom the heavens and the earth belong.

* *

His saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: Not equal among you, O people, are those who believed before the conquest of Makkah and emigrated.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾, he said: he believed and spent, meaning: the one who emigrated is not like the one who did not emigrate.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest﴾, he says: those who believed.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, who said: he says other than that.

And others said: By "the conquest" is meant the conquest of Makkah, and by "spending" is meant spending in jihad against the polytheists.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to each Allah has promised the best﴾, he said: There were two fightings, one of which was superior to the other, and there were two spendings, one of which was superior to the other; spending and fighting before the conquest, "the conquest of Makkah," were superior to spending and fighting after it.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿before the conquest﴾, he said: the conquest of Makkah.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding this verse: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest﴾, he said: the conquest of Makkah.

And others said: By "the conquest" in this place is meant the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah.

Mention of those who said that:

Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abd Allah related to us, from Dawud, from Amir, who said: What separates the two emigrations is the conquest of al-Hudaybiyah. His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought ...﴾ the verse.

Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, regarding this verse, His saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought﴾, he said: the conquest of al-Hudaybiyah; he said: "What separates the two 'umrahs is the conquest of al-Hudaybiyah."

Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, who said: "What separates the two emigrations is the conquest of al-Hudaybiyah." And there was revealed: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest﴾ ... to ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾. They said: O Messenger of Allah, is it a conquest? Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him, and he will have a generous reward?﴾ (57:11)

His Exalted remembrance says: Who is it that spends in the way of Allah in this world, seeking reward in his expenditure and desiring what is with Allah? That is the goodly loan. He says: his Lord will multiply for him the loan he lent, by his spending in His way, so that He makes for him one become seven hundred.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say concerning His words ﴿who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾ that it is like the saying of the Arabs: "I have a loan of truth (qarḍ ṣidq) with you," and "a loan of evil (qarḍ sū')," when one does good or evil to them. He recited as evidence a verse of al-Shanfara:

"We will repay Salamān ibn Mufrij his loan, for what their hands had sent forward, and they slipped."

[[The author attributes the verse to al-Shanfara. Salāmān ibn Mufrij is a tribe of the Arabs. ﴿And he will have a generous reward﴾ means: He will have a reward and a recompense that is generous. By that reward is meant Paradise. We have already mentioned the reports from the people of interpretation on this matter earlier, in a way that suffices without repeating it.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 12:

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when you see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands, (it will be said): "Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally. That is the great triumph."﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿On the Day when you see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: On the Day when you see the believing men and women, their light shining before them and on their right hands.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿On the Day when you see the believing men and the believing women﴾ ... the verse. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Among the believers is one whose light shines from Medina to Aden Abyan and San'a, and beyond that; and among the believers is one whose light shines only as far as the place of his feet."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, similarly.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father mention, from al-Minhal, from 'Amr, from Qays ibn Sakan, from 'Abdullah, who said: "They are given their light according to the measure of their deeds. Among them is one whose light is given like a palm tree, and among them is one whose light is given like a standing man, and the one with the least light has it on his thumb: it goes out once and flares up once."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: On the Day when you see the believing men and women, their faith and guidance running before them, and on their right hands: their books.

Mention of those who said that:

- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿their light running before them and on their right hands﴾: "Their books." Allah says: As for the one given his book in his right hand, and as for their light, it is their guidance.

The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the opinion we have mentioned from al-Dahhak. This is because, if by that He meant the known radiance, the report would not single out running before them and on their right hands to the exclusion of the left, since the light that the believers are given in the Hereafter illuminates everything around them. And the fact that Allah, the Majestic, specifically reports their running before them and on their right hands, rather than the left, indicates that something other than radiance is meant, even though they are not free of radiance.

So the interpretation of the speech, given that the matter is as we have described, is: "And to each Allah has promised the best," on the Day when you see the believing men and women, the reward of their faith and righteous deeds running before them, and in their right hands their books of deeds fluttering.

By His words ﴿running﴾ He means: proceeding. The "ba'" in His words ﴿and on their right hands﴾ is in the sense of "fi" (in). Some grammarians of Basra said: the "ba'" in His words ﴿and on their right hands﴾ is in the sense of "'ala" (upon), meaning upon their right hands.

* *

His words ﴿On the Day when you see﴾:

This is connected to the promise ("wa'd").

* *

His words ﴿Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It is said to them: Your good news today, O believers, which you were promised, is gardens beneath which rivers flow; so rejoice in them.

* *

His words ﴿abiding therein﴾:

He says: remaining in the gardens, not moving away from them nor transferring from them.

* *

His words ﴿That is the great triumph﴾:

He says: their eternal abiding in the gardens that He described is the great success that they were seeking, after being saved from the punishment of Allah, and entering the Garden to abide therein eternally.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the hypocritical men and hypocritical women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Return you behind you and seek light." So a wall with a gate will be struck between them; its inner side will have mercy, and its outer side will have torment from before it.﴾ (13) ﴿They will call to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted, and false hopes deluded you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deluded you concerning Allah."﴾ (14)

His exalted remembrance says: That is the great triumph, on a day when the hypocritical men and hypocritical women will say to those who believed in Allah and His messengers, "Wait for us" (the word "day" is linked to "the triumph").

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿انْظُرُونَا﴾ (unzurūnā). The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it as ﴿انْظُرُونَا﴾ with a connected alif, meaning "wait for us." The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as ﴿أنْظُرُونا﴾ with a cut alif, from anzhartu, meaning "delay for us." Al-Farra' mentioned that the Arabs say "anzirnī" while meaning "wait for me a little," and he cited the verse of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm: "Abā Hind, do not hasten against us, and wait for us, we will inform you of the certainty."

[This verse is from the Mu'allaqa of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm al-Taghlibī (see the commentaries of al-Zawzanī and al-Tibrīzī), addressing ʿAmr ibn Hind, king of al-Hira. It is one of al-Farra's evidences in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an. He said, on the verse "Wait for us": Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and Hamza read "anzirūnā" from anzartu. The rest of the readers read "unzurūnā" with a light alif. The meaning of "unzurūnā" is "wait for us," and the meaning of "anzirūnā" is "delay for us," as He said: "Give me respite until the day they are raised." The Arabs may say "anzirnī" while meaning "wait for me," in support of Yahya's reading. The poet said: "Abā Hind... the verse," so the meaning here is: wait a little for us, we will inform you, since there is no delay here, rather it is listening, like your saying to a man: listen to me until I inform you. End.

In al-Lisan (under nazara): "al-naẓar" means waiting. It is said: nazartu fulānan and intaẓartuhu have the same meaning. When you say intazartu, your verb does not exceed you, and its meaning is: I stopped and took my time. From this is His saying, "Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light," which was read both as unzurūnā and anzirūnā with a cut alif. Whoever reads "unzurūnā" with a damma on the alif means "wait for us," and whoever reads "anzirūnā" means "delay for us." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "anzirūnā" is also "wait for us," and from it is ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's verse: "Abā Hind... the verse." End.]

He said: So the meaning here is: wait a little for us, that we may inform you, since there is no delay here; it is only listening, like your saying to a man: listen to me until I inform you.

The correct recitation in my view is the connected form, because that is what is well known in the speech of the Arabs when "wait for us" is meant, and there is no sense of delay in this context, so it would not be said "anzirūnā" with an opened alif and a hamza.

* *

His saying: ﴿Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light﴾

He says: "that we may kindle our torches from your light." The qabas is the flame.

* *

His saying: ﴿It will be said, "Return you behind you and seek light"﴾

His majestic praise says: They will be answered by being told: return to where you came from, and seek for yourselves light there, for you have no way to acquire from our light.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

When the believers saw the light, they headed toward it, and the light was a guide from Allah to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers had set off, they followed them, but Allah cast darkness over the hypocrites. Then they said: "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light, for we were with you in the world." The believers said: "Return from where you came, out of the darkness, and seek the light there."

– Ḥudithtu ʿan al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying: ﴿On the Day when the hypocritical men and hypocritical women say to those who believed...﴾ the verse. Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: While the people were in darkness... and he mentioned something similar.

* *

His saying: ﴿So a wall with a gate will be struck between them; its inner side will have mercy, and its outer side will have torment from before it.﴾

His exalted remembrance says: So Allah struck between the believers and the hypocrites a wall, which is a barrier between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

– Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, he said: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, he said: al-Ḥasan related to us, he said: Waraqāʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿with a wall that has a gate﴾: "Like the veil in al-Aʿrāf."

– Bishr related to us, he said: Yazīd related to us, he said: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying: ﴿So a wall with a gate will be struck between them﴾: the wall is a barrier between Paradise and Hell.

– Yūnus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So a wall with a gate will be struck between them﴾: "This is the wall that Allah mentioned: ﴿and between them is a veil﴾."

It has also been said that this wall is at Bayt al-Maqdis, near the Valley of Hell.

Those who said that:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the hypocritical men and hypocritical women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Return you behind you and seek light." So a wall with a gate will be struck between them; its inner side will have mercy, and its outer side will have torment from before it.﴾ (13) ﴿They will call to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted, and false hopes deluded you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deluded you concerning Allah."﴾ (14)

His exalted remembrance says: That is the great triumph, on a day when the hypocritical men and hypocritical women will say to those who believed in Allah and His messengers, "Wait for us" (the word "day" is linked to "the triumph").

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿انْظُرُونَا﴾ (unzurūnā). The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it as ﴿انْظُرُونَا﴾ with a connected alif, meaning "wait for us." The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as ﴿أنْظُرُونا﴾ with a cut alif, from anzhartu, meaning "delay for us." Al-Farra' mentioned that the Arabs say "anzirnī" while meaning "wait for me a little," and he cited the verse of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm: "Abā Hind, do not hasten against us, and wait for us, we will inform you of the certainty."

[This verse is from the Mu'allaqa of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm al-Taghlibī (see the commentaries of al-Zawzanī and al-Tibrīzī), addressing ʿAmr ibn Hind, king of al-Hira. It is one of al-Farra's evidences in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an. He said, on the verse "Wait for us": Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and Hamza read "anzirūnā" from anzartu. The rest of the readers read "unzurūnā" with a light alif. The meaning of "unzurūnā" is "wait for us," and the meaning of "anzirūnā" is "delay for us," as He said: "Give me respite until the day they are raised." The Arabs may say "anzirnī" while meaning "wait for me," in support of Yahya's reading. The poet said: "Abā Hind... the verse," so the meaning here is: wait a little for us, we will inform you, since there is no delay here, rather it is listening, like your saying to a man: listen to me until I inform you. End.

In al-Lisan (under nazara): "al-naẓar" means waiting. It is said: nazartu fulānan and intaẓartuhu have the same meaning. When you say intazartu, your verb does not exceed you, and its meaning is: I stopped and took my time. From this is His saying, "Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light," which was read both as unzurūnā and anzirūnā with a cut alif. Whoever reads "unzurūnā" with a damma on the alif means "wait for us," and whoever reads "anzirūnā" means "delay for us." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "anzirūnā" is also "wait for us," and from it is ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's verse: "Abā Hind... the verse." End.]

He said: So the meaning here is: wait a little for us, that we may inform you, since there is no delay here; it is only listening, like your saying to a man: listen to me until I inform you.

The correct recitation in my view is the connected form, because that is what is well known in the speech of the Arabs when "wait for us" is meant, and there is no sense of delay in this context, so it would not be said "anzirūnā" with an opened alif and a hamza.

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "Has the time not come for those who believe" — has it not come near for those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger that their hearts should soften to the remembrance of Allah, so that their hearts humble themselves before Him, and to what has been revealed of the truth, which is this Qur'an that He sent down to His Messenger ﷺ.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah﴾, he said: their hearts should obey.

It was mentioned to us that Shaddad ibn Aws used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first thing that will be taken from the people is humility (khushu')."

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Shaddad ibn Aws used to say: The first thing that will be taken from people is humility.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 17–18:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, that you might understand.﴾ (17) ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and [those who] lend to Allah a goodly loan – it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.﴾ (18)

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿Know﴾, O people, ﴿that Allah gives life to the earth﴾ that is dead and produces nothing, ﴿after its death﴾, meaning: after its decay and effacement. He says: Just as We bring this dead earth back to life after its effacement, so too do We guide the human being who has strayed from the truth to the truth, granting him success and making him upright in faith, so that he becomes a believer after his disbelief, and one guided after his straying.

* *

And His saying: ﴿We have certainly made clear to you the signs, that you might understand﴾

He says: We have certainly made clear to you the proofs and arguments, so that you may understand.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity (al-mussaddiqin) and the women who give charity (al-mussaddiqat)﴾

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the metropolitan cities recited it with the sad and dal both shaddah (doubled), except Ibn Kathir and Asim, with the meaning that al-mutasaddiqin and al-mutasaddiqat, then the taa is assimilated into the saad, making it a doubled saad, as it is said: ﴿O you who are wrapped (al-muzzammil)﴾, meaning al-mutazammil. Ibn Kathir and Asim recited: ﴿Indeed, the men who are charitable (al-mutasaddiqin) and the women who are charitable (al-mutasaddiqat)﴾ with the saad unshaddah and the dal shaddah, meaning: indeed, those who affirm the truth of Allah and His Messenger.

The most correct of the opinions regarding this, in my view, is to say: these are two well-known recitations, and the meaning of each of them is sound, so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

The interpretation of the speech, then, according to the recitation of the one who read it with doubling in both letters, namely the saad and the dal, is: the men who give charity from their wealth and the women who give charity, ﴿and lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾, meaning: by spending in His way and in what He has commanded to be spent upon, or what He has recommended, ﴿it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward﴾. He says: Allah will multiply for them the loans they have lent Him, and will repay them their reward on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And they will have a noble reward﴾, He says: and they will have a reward from Allah for their charity, and their loans to Him, a noble reward, and that is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 19:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful ones (al-siddiqun) and the martyrs (al-shuhada') with their Lord. They will have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Those who acknowledge the oneness of Allah and His sending of messengers, who affirm the messengers and believe in what they brought from their Lord, they are the truthful ones (al-siddiqun).

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding this. Some of them said: "And the martyrs with their Lord" is separated from what precedes it, and the report about those who believe in Allah and His messengers ends at His saying: ﴿the truthful ones (al-siddiqun)﴾, and al-siddiqun is in the nominative case by His saying "they are" (hum). Then a new statement begins about the martyrs, and it is said: "And the martyrs with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light." The martyrs (al-shuhada') in their statement are in the nominative case by His saying: ﴿for them is their reward and their light﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful ones﴾, he said: this is separated. ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light﴾.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq: ﴿They are the truthful ones and the martyrs with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light﴾, he said: it is for the martyrs specifically.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, he said: it is specifically for the martyrs.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Duha: ﴿They are the truthful ones﴾, then he resumed speech and said: "And the martyrs with their Lord."

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful ones﴾: this is separated. Allah named them truthful ones because they believed in Allah and affirmed His messengers. Then He said: ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light﴾: this is separated.

Others said: Rather, His saying "and the martyrs" is a description of those who believe in Allah and His messengers. They said: the report about those who believe ends at His saying: ﴿and the martyrs with their Lord﴾, then a new statement begins about what they have, so it is said: "For them is their reward and their light."

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, he said: Abu Qays informed us that he heard Hudhayl narrate, he said: They mentioned the martyrs, and 'Abd Allah said: "A man fights for remembrance, a man fights to be seen in his place, a man fights for the world, a man fights for reputation, a man fights for booty." Shu'bah said something with this meaning: "And a man fights seeking the face of Allah, and a man dies on his bed and he is a martyr." And 'Abd Allah recited this verse: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful ones and the martyrs with their Lord﴾.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, and Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful ones and the martyrs with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light﴾, he said: every believer is a martyr, then he recited it.

* Salih ibn Harb Abu Ma'mar related to me, he said: Isma'il ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Ibn 'Ajlan related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The believers of my community are martyrs." He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful ones and the martyrs with their Lord﴾.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿The truthful ones and the martyrs with their Lord﴾, he said: by faith against themselves in Allah.

Others said: The martyrs with their Lord in this place are the prophets, who bear witness over their nations, from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾

The view that is most correct in my judgment is the view of the one who said: the statement and report about those who believe ends at His saying: ﴿they are the truthful ones﴾, and that His saying: ﴿and the martyrs with their Lord﴾ is a report beginning a new subject about the martyrs.

We said that this is the most correct of these views because it is the most prevalent of its meanings on the surface, and because faith does not, in common usage, make the believer be called a martyr in a sense other than its own, unless it is meant as a witness to what he believed in and affirmed, in which case that would be a possible reading, though somewhat distant, since that is not the familiar meaning of the word when used without a connecting clause. Therefore the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and the martyrs with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light﴾ is: and the martyrs who were killed in the way of Allah, or who perished in His way, with their Lord, for them is Allah's reward to them in the Hereafter and their light.

* *

And His saying: ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Those who disbelieve in Allah and deny His proofs and arguments, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.

The exegesis on His saying, exalted is He: "Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement, adornment and boasting among yourselves, and competition in wealth and children. It is like rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval. And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion" (57:20).

His exalted saying means: Know, O people, that the enjoyment of the life of this world, which is hastened for you, is nothing but play and amusement by which you take delight, and adornment with which you beautify yourselves, and boasting among you, where some of you boast over others with what they have acquired of its finery. "And competition in wealth and children" – He, exalted is His remembrance, means: and some of you vie with one another in multiplying wealth and children.

"It is like rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up" – He, exalted is His remembrance, means: then that vegetation withers. "Then you see it turning yellow" after it had been green and fresh.

* *

As for His saying: "Then it becomes debris" (ḥuṭāman).

He, exalted is His remembrance, means: then that vegetation becomes debris; by this He means that it becomes dry, crumbling vegetation. "And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment" – He, exalted is His remembrance, means: and in the Hereafter there is severe punishment for the disbelievers. "And forgiveness from Allah and approval" – for the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger.

As for what has been transmitted:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement..." to the end of the verse, he said: "People have come to these two phrases in the Hereafter."

Some of the scholars of Arabic used to say, regarding His saying: "And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and approval": it mentions what is in this world, and that it is as described; as for the Hereafter, it is either punishment or Paradise. He said: The "wa" (and) in it is in the sense of "aw" (or), and both have the same function.

* *

As for His saying: "And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion."

He, exalted is His remembrance, means: and the adornment of the life of this world, which is hastened for you, O people, is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.

Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 21:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾ (57:21)

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Race﴾, O people, ﴿to﴾ a deed that makes you deserving of ﴿forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth. It has been prepared﴾ — this Garden — ﴿for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers﴾, meaning: those who affirmed the oneness of Allah and confirmed His messengers.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾

He, whose praise is great, says: this Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, which Allah has prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers, is a bounty of Allah which He has bestowed upon the believers. Allah gives His bounty to whom He wills of His creation, and He is the possessor of great bounty over them, by having spread provision for them in this world, bestowed upon them blessings, made them aware of the place of gratitude, and then rewarded them in the Hereafter for obedience with what He described as having prepared for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 22:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or among yourselves but it is in a Record before We bring it into being﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Whatever calamity befalls you, O people, on earth, by way of drought and dearth, and the ruin of its crops and their destruction, ﴿nor among yourselves﴾ by ailments, aches and sicknesses, ﴿but it is in a Record﴾, meaning: but it is in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), ﴿before We bring it into being﴾. He says: before We bring the souls into being, meaning: before We create them. It is said: God has brought this thing into being (bara'a), meaning: He created it, so He is its Creator (bari').

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or among yourselves but it is in a Record before We bring it into being﴾, he said: it is a matter that has already been completed before We brought the soul into being.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth﴾: as for the calamity of the earth, it is the years of drought. As for "among yourselves": these are the illnesses and aches. ﴿Before We bring it into being﴾: before We create it.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth﴾, he said: it is the years of drought. ﴿Nor among yourselves﴾, he said: the pains and illnesses. He said: We have been told that no one is struck by the scratch of a twig, nor the stumbling of a foot, nor the throbbing of a vein, except because of a sin, and what He pardons is more.

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Mansur ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I was sitting with al-Hasan, when a man said: Ask him about His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or among yourselves but it is in a Record before We bring it into being﴾. So I asked him about it, and he said: Glory be to God, and who doubts this? Every calamity between heaven and earth is in the Book of God before the soul is brought into being.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or among yourselves but it is in a Record before We bring it into being﴾: it is a matter that has already been completed, ﴿before We bring it into being﴾: before We bring the souls into being.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding the saying of God, may His praise be exalted: ﴿in a Record before We bring it into being﴾: before We create it. He said: The calamities, the provision, and all things that you love and dislike, God has completed all of that before He brings the souls into being and creates them.

Others said: What is meant by this is: whatever calamity befalls in religion or in worldly life.

Those who said that:

'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or among yourselves but it is in a Record before We bring it into being﴾, he says: in religion and in worldly life, ﴿but it is in a Record﴾: before We create them.

The grammarians differed concerning the meaning of "fi" (in) that comes after the saying "illa" (but). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it means, and God knows best: "illa hiya fi kitab" (but it is in a Record), so the omission of the pronoun is permissible. He said: "This is not but..." means "this is not but he," that is, "illa huwa". Another of them said: His saying ﴿in a Record﴾ is connected to "what befalls", and the implicit pronoun "huwa" is not something correct. He said: His saying "in my view this is not but..." is like it, because "illa" suffices for the verb, as if he said: "there is nothing other than it".

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed that is easy for God﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, the creation of souls and the enumeration of what calamities they will encounter is easy and simple for God.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿So that you do not despair over what has escaped you, nor exult in what He has given you. And Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾ [57:23].

He, the Exalted, says: No calamity befalls you, O people, in your wealth or in yourselves, except that it is in a Book (kitab) in which it was written before We created your souls. ﴿So that you do not despair﴾ means: so that you do not grieve ﴿over what has escaped you﴾ of the worldly life, so that you do not attain it from it, ﴿nor exult in what He has given you﴾ of it.

As for the meaning of His saying ﴿what He has given you﴾: if the alif is extended (ʾātākum), then it means: with what your Lord has given you of it, granted you and made you its master; and if the alif is shortened (atākum), its meaning is: with what has come to you of it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿So that you do not despair over what has escaped you﴾ of the worldly life, ﴿nor exult in what He has given you﴾ of it.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan, who said: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, from Qays, from Sammak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿So that you do not despair over what has escaped you﴾, he said: patience at the time of calamity and gratitude at the time of blessing.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Sammak al-Bakri, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿So that you do not despair over what has escaped you﴾, he said: No one is without grief and joy, but whoever is struck by a calamity makes it patience, and whoever receives good makes it gratitude.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿So that you do not despair over what has escaped you, nor exult in what He has given you﴾, he said: Do not despair over what has escaped you of the worldly life, nor exult in what has come to you of it.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying ﴿what He has given you﴾. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Kufa read ﴿bi-mā ātākum﴾ with an extended alif, while some reciters of Basra read ﴿bi-mā atākum﴾ with a shortened alif. It seems that whoever read it with the shortened alif chose that reading because the preceding phrase was ʿalā mā fātakum (what has escaped you), not ʿalā mā afātakum, so he attached ﴿bi-mā atākum﴾ to it, and did not refer the verb to a report about Allah.

The correct view on this matter is that both are valid readings with sound meanings, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct. Although I prefer the extended alif, because most reciters read it that way. The objection raised by those who read it with the shortened alif carries no great weight, because whether it is taken as a report about Allah or as a report about other than Him, it is entirely clear to the knowledgeable hearers that it is the act of Allah, the Exalted. What has escaped one from the world is what escaped him by the decree and judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and what one attains of it is what he attains by the foreordainment and decree of Allah. His Majesty has made this clear to whoever understands Him in His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being﴾ [57:22]. So He informed that what escapes from it escaped them by His causing it to escape from them, and what they attain of it they attained by His giving it to them, and that this is preserved for them in a Book before He created them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾:

He says: And Allah does not love every proud person who is arrogant about what he has been given of the world, boasting of it over the people.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people. And whoever turns away—indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (57:24)

His Exalted Remembrance says: Indeed Allah does not love every arrogant boaster, those who are stingy with what they have been given in this world, out of their conceit in it and their boasting about it before people. So they withhold from paying out the right of Allah which He has made obligatory upon them in it, and they are tight-fisted with it. And along with their stinginess with it, they also enjoin people to be stingy.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whoever turns away—indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾

His Exalted Remembrance says: And whoever turns his back, turning away from the admonition of Allah, ﴿indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ His Exalted Remembrance says: whoever turns his back, turning away from the admonition of Allah, abandoning the act of what He has called him to, namely spending in His way, exulting in what he has been given of this world, proud of it, boastful, and miserly. Indeed Allah is free of need of his wealth and his spending, and free of need of anyone else among all His creation, and praiseworthy toward His creation for the blessings He has bestowed upon them.

The scholars of Arabic (ahl al-ʿArabiyya, the grammarians) differed concerning the position of the response (jawab) to His words: ﴿Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people﴾. Some of them said: it is dispensed with by the reports that are similar to them, and which they have in the Qur'an, as in His words: ﴿Had there been a Qur'an by which mountains were set in motion, or the earth were cut asunder, or the dead were made to speak...﴾, and there is no predicate (khabar) in this place. Allah knows best what He sends down; it is as He sent it down, or as He willed it to be. And another of the grammarians said: the predicate has come in the verse before this one, (those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people, and whoever turns away—indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy), joined as two conditional clauses upon one condition, and their response is one, just as you say: "If you stand, and if you do well, I will give you," not that the predicate has been omitted.

The reciters differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited ﴿fa-inna Allaha al-Ghaniyyu﴾ with the word "huwa" (he) omitted from the speech, and likewise it is written without "huwa" in their codices. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited ﴿fa-inna Allaha huwa al-Ghaniyyu al-Hamid﴾, with "huwa" affirmed in the recitation, and likewise "huwa" is in their codices.

The correct position is that these are two well-known recitations, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for people, and that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty.﴾ (57:25)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We sent Our messengers with the detailed clarifications and proofs, and We sent down with them the Book, containing the rulings and laws, and the Balance, containing justice.

As related:

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿the Book and the Balance﴾, he said: "The Balance is justice."

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ [[perhaps: "and the Balance, the Balance with truth"]]; he said: "The Balance is that by which people act and conduct their affairs in this world, of their livelihoods, in which they take and give, taking by a scale and giving by a scale, knowing what they take and what they give. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 28:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Says God, dhikruhu (may He be remembered): O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger from among the People of the Two Books, the Torah and the Gospel, fear Allah by performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience, and believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

As:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾: he means those who believed from among the People of the Book.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾: he means those among the People of the Book who believed.

* *

And His words: ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾

He will give you two portions of reward, for your belief in Jesus (ﷺ) and the prophets before Muhammad (ﷺ), and then your belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) when he was sent as a prophet. The root of kifl (portion) is ḥaẓẓ (share); its origin is what the rider is seated upon (iktafala), which holds him and keeps him from falling; he says: this kifl will protect you from the punishment, just as the kifl protects the rider from falling.

Commentators have said what is similar to what we have said concerning this.

Those who said so:

Abu 'Ammar al-Marwazi related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: two rewards, for their belief in Jesus (ﷺ) and their affirmation of the Torah and the Gospel, and their belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and their affirmation of him.

He said: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: two rewards: their belief in Muhammad (ﷺ), and their belief in Jesus (ﷺ), and the Torah and the Gospel.

And by the same chain from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas; and Harun ibn 'Antarah, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: two rewards.

Ali related to us, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he says: two portions.

He said: Mihran related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ja'far with seventy riders to al-Najashi, inviting him. He arrived before him, invited him, and he responded and believed in him. When they were about to depart, some people from among those in his realm who had believed, forty men, said: "Permit us, and we will come to this Prophet and submit to him, and we will assist these (Muslims) at sea, for we know the sea better than they do." So they came with Ja'far to the Prophet (ﷺ), who was preparing for the Battle of Uhud. When they saw the destitution and severe condition of the Muslims, they asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission, saying: "O Prophet of Allah, we have wealth, and we see the destitution of the Muslims; if you permit us, we will go back, bring our wealth, and console the Muslims with it." He permitted them, so they departed, brought their wealth, and consoled the Muslims with it. Then Allah revealed concerning them ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾ ... to His words ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾, and that was the spending with which they consoled the Muslims. When the People of the Book who had not believed heard His words ﴿They will be given their reward twice for what they endured﴾, they boasted over the Muslims, saying: "O company of Muslims, whoever among us believes in your Book and our Book, has his reward doubled, and whoever does not believe in your Book has a reward like your reward. So what is your superiority over us?" Then Allah revealed ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾, so He gave them their reward, and increased them in light and forgiveness. Then He said ﴿so that the People of the Book may know﴾. Thus Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited it: ﴿so that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything﴾.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: two portions.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: the two portions are two rewards, for their former belief and for the Book that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾: he means those among the People of the Book who believed, ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he says: two rewards for your belief in the former Book and in that which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: two rewards: the reward of this world and the reward of the Hereafter.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Sufyan, saying: 'Anbasah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Musa, concerning ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾: he said: the two portions are two multiples of reward in the language of the Abyssinians.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Sha'bi, who said: People on the Day of Resurrection are in four states: a man who was a believer in Jesus, then believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), has two rewards. A man who was a disbeliever in Jesus, then believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), has one reward. A man who was a disbeliever in Jesus, then disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), returns with anger upon anger. And a man who was a disbeliever in Jesus from among the polytheists of the Arabs, who died in his disbelief before Muhammad, returns with anger.

Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid related to me, saying: my father informed me, saying: I asked Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz about the kifl, how much is it? He said: three hundred and fifty good deeds, and the two kifls: seven hundred good deeds. Sa'id said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) asked a rabbi from the rabbis of the Jews: "What is the greatest multiplication of a good deed for you?" He said: "A kifl of three hundred and fifty good deeds." He said: 'Umar praised Allah that He had given us two kifls. Then Sa'id mentioned the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in Surah al-Hadid ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾. I said to him: "Are the two kifls on Friday like this?" He said: "Yes."

It is in accordance with what we have said on this matter that the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is authentically transmitted.

Those who said so:

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Rashid related to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three people will be given their reward twice: a man who believed in the former Book and the latter Book; a man who had a slave-girl, whom he educated and educated well, then freed her and married her; and a slave who worshipped his Lord well and advised his master."

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, saying: Salih ibn Salih al-Hamdani related to me, from 'Amir, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad related to me, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Salih ibn Salih, who heard al-Sha'bi narrate, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similarly.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Furat informed us, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id said: Nafi' informed us that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Your lifespans in comparison to the lifespans of those who passed before among the nations are like the period between the afternoon prayer and sunset. Your example and the example of the Jews and the Christians is like a man who hired workers and said: 'Who will work for me from morning until midday for a qirat each?' So the Jews worked. Then he said: 'Who will work for me from midday until the afternoon prayer for a qirat each?' So the Christians worked. Then he said: 'Who will work for me from the afternoon prayer until sunset for two qirats each?' Then you worked."

Ali ibn Sahl related to me, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, that he heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The example of this community, or he said my community, and the example of the Jews and the Christians, is like a man who said: 'Who will work for me from morning until midday for a qirat?' The Jews said: 'We will.' So they worked. He said: 'Who will work for me from midday until the afternoon prayer for a qirat?' The Christians said: 'We will.' So they worked. And you, the Muslims, work from the afternoon prayer until night for two qirats." The Jews and the Christians became angry and said: "We did more work and received less reward." He said: "Have I wronged you in your wages at all?" They said: "No." He said: "That is My bounty, which I give to whom I will."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: al-Layth and Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, that he said: I witnessed the sermon of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage. He said many good and beautiful words, and among them was: "Whoever embraces Islam from among the People of the Two Books, he has his reward twice, and he has what we have, and upon him is what is upon us. And whoever embraces Islam from among the polytheists, he has his reward, and he has what we have, and upon him is what is upon us."

* *

And His words: ﴿and make for you a light by which you will walk﴾

The commentators differed concerning what is meant by light in this place. Some of them said: it means the Qur'an.

Those who said so:

Abu 'Ammar al-Marwazi related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿and make for you a light by which you will walk﴾: he said: the criterion (al-furqan) and their following of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿and make for you a light by which you will walk﴾: he said: the criterion, and their following of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿and make for you a light by which you will walk﴾: he said: the Qur'an.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata', from Sa'id, similarly.

Others said: the light in this place means guidance.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿by which you will walk﴾: he said: guidance.

The most correct of the sayings concerning this is that it should be said: God, dhikruhu, promised these people that He would make for them a light by which they would walk, namely the Qur'an together with following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which is a light for whoever believes in and affirms them both, and guidance; for whoever believes in that has been guided.

* *

And His words: ﴿and forgive you﴾

He says: and He will pardon you for your sins, veiling them over you. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: God, dhikruhu, says: Allah is possessor of forgiveness and mercy.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 29:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ (29).

His exalted remembrance says, addressing the believers among the People of the Scripture who believed in Him and in Muhammad ﷺ: your Lord does this so that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah which He has given you and bestowed upon you, for they used to see that Allah had preferred them over all creation. So Allah, mighty is His praise, informed them that He had given the community of Muhammad ﷺ bounty and honour that He had not given them, and that the People of the Scripture envied the believers when there was revealed His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. So Allah, mighty and majestic, said: I did that so that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾ ... the verse. He said: When this verse was revealed, the People of the Scripture envied the Muslims because of it, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power﴾ ... the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: "The likeness of us and of the two previous People of the Book is like a man who hired labourers, who work until the night for a qirat. When midday came, they grew weary of his work and became bored, so he settled with them according to that measure. Then he hired other labourers to work for him until night for two qirats, to complete the rest of his work. It was said to him: What is the matter with these, who are fewer in work and greater in wage? He said: Am I not free to give to whom I wish? So I hope that we are the people of the two qirats."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿a double portion of His mercy﴾, he said: It has reached us that when it was revealed, the People of the Scripture envied the Muslims, so Allah revealed ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾.

- Abu 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know﴾: those who listen in secret. ﴿that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

It has been said that ﴿li-allā yaʿlama﴾ means only "li-yaʿlama" (so that he may know). It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is ﴿li-kay yaʿlama ahlu al-kitab allā yaqdirūn﴾, because the Arabs make "lā" (no) an extra particle in every speech in which a negation not explicitly stated occurs at its beginning or end, like His saying, in an implied negation not explicitly stated: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾, and His saying: ﴿And what makes you perceive that when it comes they will not believe?﴾, and His saying: ﴿And it is forbidden to a city which We have destroyed﴾ ... the verse, and the meaning of that is: We destroyed it, that they do not return.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Ghanawi informed us, saying: Khattab ibn 'Abdullah said regarding ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾.

- He said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr used to say ﴿li-kaylā yaʿlama ahlu al-kitab﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾

His exalted remembrance says: and that they may know that bounty is in the hand of Allah, not in theirs, nor in the hand of any other creature, ﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾, meaning: He gives His bounty to whomever He wills of His creation, and that is not for anyone other than Him, ﴿and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾, meaning: His exalted remembrance says: Allah is the possessor of bounty over His creation, the great in His bounty.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Hadid.
